goal: The developer builds a Claude Code plugin whose roles work together to make something, with which its users achieve what they're after.

intents.what: Placing a file of the plugin, does the developer see which part takes the form Claude Code fixes and which holds the work's own knowledge, so that each job lies in one place and what the plugin knows outlives the agent it runs on?

Starting a role, does the developer have it hold its whole part before its first call, each file the part names found wherever Claude Code installs the plugin, so that the role works from all it has to do?

Writing a role's part, does the developer put in it only what the role has to do and which parts of the best practice it uses, so that the role takes the practices as the steps of its work and no copy of them drifts?
Splitting the work into roles, does the developer give each job a role of its own with only what the job needs, so that nothing from other work leads a role astray?

Following a run from the person's request, does the developer see the main conversation start each role, put each point a role has for the person to them as given, and take the answer back word for word, so that no agent between them rewords a question or sums up an answer?

Starting, resuming, or ending a role, can a machine check what passes between the main conversation and the role, so that each role works from the run's values and the person's own words, and the run moves on by the result that the role gave?
Choosing how to keep a file that the plugin reads, does the developer keep it in a form that a script checks, so that no role or person acts on a file out of form?
Following a run from a role's end to the next start, does every run take the same moves, so that a stopped run goes on from its last move?

Where an instruction alone doesn't hold a step, does the developer have a hook stop the role and tell it the step again when it drifts, so that the plugin's users get on every run what the step makes, not only on the runs where the role kept to it?
Reading what a check gave, does the developer tell a pass from a check that couldn't run, so that the plugin's users and its developer never act on a pass that no check made?

Checking a role's work, does the developer have a script or the project's own tools check all that a machine can see, so that the work reaches its user with no fault that a machine could find, and no round of an AI goes to one?
Writing a file as it runs, does the plugin put it where its user chooses whether git keeps it, so that a stopped run leaves nothing behind and an update loses nothing?
Running on a user's machine, does the plugin need only what's already there, so that it runs wherever git does?
Needing code that another plugin of the marketplace has, does the developer keep it in one place, so that they write, test, and fix it once?
Having another plugin do a job, does the developer take the part of it that does the job, so that the other runs as its makers built and tested it and nobody writes it again?
Reaching a point that's the caller's, such as a merge, does the plugin take it as approved only by the caller's own act, so that no AI decides for them?
Meeting a point that the work needs, does a role put to the person only what's theirs, one point at a time with a recommendation, so that a point settled before the work doesn't come back as rework?
When something outside the work stops a role, such as a permission or a tool, does the role ask for it and go on with the rest, so that the work stays checked on the terms its purpose set?
Reading what the plugin says and writes, do the person and the repository's later readers each find it in their own language, so that the person approves what they read?
Before the work reaches its user, does a role that didn't make it check it in the user's place, so that the work's user gets what they're after and not what its maker meant?
Once a run ends, does the plugin take in what fell short and why, so that a lesson met once improves every later run?

Testing the plugin at each level that its architecture names, does the developer know what of Claude Code to run real and what to stand in for, so that the developer learns of a broken path before a push reaches users, and the trials meet what users meet?
Installing the plugin, does each user get a manifest that Claude Code reads, so that the install never fails on its form?
Deciding whether to update, does a user find what changed for them in a version they get, so that they update knowing what it gives?

Coming to the plugin, does a would-be user find in the manifest's description what they achieve with it, and its user a README made for them, so that they choose to install it knowing what it gives, and learn from the README what they achieve with it and how?

Asking for the work in their own words, does a person reach the plugin's skill, and does each of its agents start only from that skill, so that the person gets a run of the plugin without knowing its command, and no role runs outside the run that its routes hold?
Using a plugin built by this best practice, do its users achieve what they're after?

practices.thinking: Skills, agents, hooks, and scripts take the form Claude Code fixes, each named as its caller calls it, such as the command a person types, and hand the job to the file in `domain/` that does it. `domain/` holds the knowledge of the work in one folder, with no folders split by role, and names no tool of an agent, such as the Agent tool or `AskUserQuestion`: only the entries name them. What only the developers need, such as the tests and the architecture, lies outside the plugin's folder, as installing copies only that folder. A developer then finds a job where the structure puts it, two entries to one job don't drift apart, and what the plugin knows outlives the agent it runs on, as [hexagonal architecture](https://alistair.cockburn.us/hexagonal-architecture/) says. The plugin rests on its code and its prompts, so each passes by its own best practice before the plugin does: the code in `domain/` and `scripts/` by the [code best practice](../code/best-practice.md), and the prompts, the entries and the parts in `domain/`, by the [prompt best practice](../prompt/best-practice.md). In a plan, the plugin's deliverable names in its preconditions each part it rests on: its code, its prompts, and each plugin it takes a part from, such as Lane for its guard. A plugin with no prompts, such as Lane, names no prompt among them. The plugin then starts only once each part it rests on has passed.

steps.text: Grep `domain/` for the name of each tool of an agent, and move each line it finds to the entry that uses the tool.

practices.thinking: A role works from all it has to do only when it holds its whole part from its first call. Claude Code makes an agent's body its system prompt and reads no other file into it. It puts the plugin's folder in place of `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` only in an entry's own body, not in what the Bash tool runs nor in a file that Read reads, as [environment variables](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/manifest-reference#environment-variables) says. After `/compact`, a part that a skill names comes back whole, while the skill's own body survives only as the summary retells it. So the main conversation reads the skill's part whole first. An agent's part is one file in `domain/` that its entry names, and it reaches the agent whole as the agent starts, which the guard of Q9 gives.

steps.text: Have each entry's body say that the plugin's folder is `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` and name the role's part in `domain/`, and have the part name each file as `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}/<path>`.
Have the skill's body make the main conversation read its part whole first, and have each agent's body say that the agent gets its part as it starts, as the template's `agents/role.md` says.

practices.thinking: A role's part says what the role has to do, what a machine can see once it's done, what it's given, the best practice and the intents whose practices it carries out, and what it gives as it ends, as `domain/role.md` shows. The steps of the work are those practices. The part names them by their intents, so the steps adapter of Q9 gives them to the guard, which holds the role to them one by one. Steps copied into a part drift from the practices they came from, and the role then follows the copy.

steps.text: Grep each part for a numbered list, and replace each step it holds with the intent whose practice the step carries out.

practices.thinking: Where a work has jobs that need different context or tools, each job has a role of its own, an agent whose `tools` name only what the job needs. A role starts in a fresh context, so nothing from other work leads it astray, as [subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents) says. Roles that run at the same time each work in a workspace of their own, such as a git worktree and a temporary folder that no other role writes, and their results join only through the one who started them, as two makers in one workspace overwrite each other's files unseen.

steps.text: Set each agent's `tools` to the tools that its part's practices use, and `background: true`, as the guard that Q9 lays counts a start only once its role ends.

practices.thinking: Where a plugin has roles, its skill makes the main conversation the orchestrator, by a part of its own in the form of `domain/command.md`. Nobody relays: the main conversation starts each role in the order that the routes of Q8 give, so each role's point reaches it, and it puts the point to the person as given and resumes the role with their answer word for word by SendMessage. It makes, judges, and decides nothing of the work. A subagent's last message reaches only the one who started it, and only the main conversation can ask the person, as [subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#available-tools) says. So an agent between them would only carry points: a point reworded on the way is a question that no role asked, and an answer summed up loses what the person meant. A resumed role keeps its whole conversation, as [resume subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#resume-subagents) says. An AI calls the plugin by the same skill, as its own orchestrator runs in the main conversation too.

steps.text: Write an architecture test that runs the skill's part through a start and a resume of each role, and check that each prompt holds only the run values and the person's words.

practices.thinking: Each role's in and out keep to JSON Schemas in `domain/`, drawn from `domain/role-in.schema.json` and `domain/role-out.schema.json`. A role starts with one JSON line of run values, which its in schema names for the guard of Q9 to hold its calls to, and resumes with a message whose first line is `The person's answer, word for word:`. It ends by giving a result, a fixed word such as `asks` or `done`, which its out schema names for the routes of Q8 to go on from, and its last message begins with `For the person:` where it holds a point for the person. A role that judges a work by questions writes its answers with the lines of the work that meet each question. A machine checks a fixed form, while words written freely leave each reader to guess.

steps.text: Write each role's two schemas, and have the script that a role runs before it gives its result hold the role's answers to them.

practices.thinking: A file that a plugin reads keeps to a schema that a script checks, such as JSON with a [JSON Schema](https://json-schema.org), with a tree nested in it, such as a design tree. A document that the plugin rewrites, such as the design tree or a round's answers, keeps such a form. A record that it only adds to, such as Lane's calls, is an append-only log, such as [JSON Lines](https://jsonlines.org), so that adding a record never rewrites what's there. A script finds a file out of form before anyone reads it, and the guard checks the nodes around a change to a tree, so the parts around it don't drift. A file that shows the form of a deliverable, such as a template or an example, keeps the deliverable's own format, as a template in another format shows a form that the deliverable can't take.

steps.text: Have each script that reads a file hold it to its schema, and write a unit test that gives the script a file out of form and checks that the script fails with the schema's error.

practices.thinking: Where a run goes in fixed moves, its routes keep the course. Lane lays them in `hooks/lanes.json` from the plugin's proposal, a JSON file kept at the root of the repository as the template's `.lane/` shows, and gives the main conversation each next start from the role that ended and the result it gave. `lay.py print` shows the routes as the main conversation meets them, before `lay.py write` lays them as Q9 says. Code follows a course the same way every time, where a conversation told the course drifts from it. Lane keeps each run's state in a file, so a compacted or stopped conversation goes on from its last move. Where a run's course changes with what it finds, the skill's part keeps the course instead.

steps.text: Write the routes in the plugin's proposal, run `lay.py print` on it, and read in what it prints that each result of each role, a dependency's role or skill among them, leads to its next start, to a wait for the person, or to the run's end.

practices.thinking: The plugin's hooks are its guard, laid by [Lane](../../../../lane/README.md) from the plugin's proposal as lanes and routes. Where a role's steps are the practices of its best practice, the proposal names a steps adapter that gives Lane those practices' steps with their traces, and lays no lane on a step of the role's part, as the part holds no numbered step. Lane lays the lanes of each step that the adapter gives from the step's trace, and gives the role each lane's sentence with its part as it starts, as [Lane's architecture](../../../../../dev/lane/architecture.md#one-wording-for-the-step-and-the-check) says and the template's `.lane/` shows. The proposal lays lanes on numbered steps only for a part that holds its own. The guard gives a role its part whole through the `SubagentStart` hook's `additionalContext`, with the plugin's folder put in place of `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`, as [a subagent's part](../../../../lane/docs/lanes.md#a-subagents-part) says. `lay.py print` shows the proposal as the guard holds it, so a part, a step, or a lane that Lane can't find shows before `lay.py write` lays any of them. A lane holds each practice step whose drift shows in a tool call or in how a role ends: its hook stops what would break the step and gives the role the step again. Branch protection or permission rules hold what's hard to undo. A hook runs every time, while an instruction is only advice. Hooks fire on the main conversation's calls with no `agent_type`, and on a role's with the role's, as [hooks](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/hooks) says, so one `hooks/hooks.json` holds both. A plugin's agent ignores `hooks`, `mcpServers`, and `permissionMode` in its own frontmatter, as [plugin agents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/components#frontmatter-fields-in-plugin-agents) says, and a `SubagentStop` hook in a skill's frontmatter didn't fire in a trial on Claude Code 2.1.318, so the plugin keeps its hooks in `hooks/hooks.json`.

steps.text: Name in each step of the best practices that the roles use a trace that a machine can check, such as a command run, a file read, or a test made. Then name in the proposal the steps adapter that gives Lane those steps, and lay a lane only on a numbered step of a part.
Run `lay.py print` on the proposal, and read in what it prints that it found each role's part and each step that the adapter gives, with its lanes.
Run `lay.py write`, which lays the proposal into the plugin's steps and `hooks/`, and removes the proposal.

practices.thinking: A check ends in one of three results: no problem, a problem, or couldn't check, such as the exit codes 0, 1, and 2. The developer decides beforehand what follows each, and tests it. A hook whose command fails stops the call, by `onFailure: block`, and a hook that finds no Python 3.9 stops each call of the plugin's own roles with why. A skipped test, a job that didn't run, or a command that failed counts as no pass, as [fail securely](https://owasp.org/www-community/Fail_securely) says. A reader takes a check that stays silent when it couldn't check for one that found nothing.

steps.text: Write a unit test for each of the three results of each check, and an architecture test that runs each hook with its script missing.

practices.thinking: A script, a hook, or the project's own tools, such as a formatter, a linter, or a type checker, check what a machine can check. An AI reads only for what no machine can. A tool finds the same thing every time, at once. An AI finds only some, and spends a round on each.

steps.text: List what each role's work must hold, and give each item a machine can see to a script that the role runs before it gives its result.

practices.thinking: A plugin writes what the user may keep in `.<plugin>/<yyyymmdd>-<name>/` at the root of the repository. It writes what it uses only while it runs, its tests' files among them, in `<plugin>/<yyyymmdd>-<name>/` in the folder that `tempfile.gettempdir()` gives, which TMPDIR moves. It writes what must outlast an update in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}`, and nothing in `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}`. One folder named after the plugin lets the user choose with one line of `.gitignore` whether git keeps it. The system clears its temporary folder, so a stopped run leaves nothing behind. An agent reads without asking only inside the working folder, as [working directories](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/permissions#working-directories) says. `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_ROOT}` changes with each update.

steps.text: Grep the plugin for each path it writes, and check that each lies under `.<plugin>/`, the system's temporary folder, or `${CLAUDE_PLUGIN_DATA}`.

practices.thinking: Where users' machines may lack other runtimes or packages, what runs there needs only a runtime that's already on them and its standard library, such as Python 3.9 or later, which is wherever git is, and a plugin installs no packages. CI runs the checks on the oldest runtime that the plugin supports and on the newest: only a run on the oldest shows that the code still runs there, and only a run on the newest shows what a new release breaks.

steps.text: Run the checks in CI on the oldest runtime that the plugin supports and on the newest, such as Python 3.9 and the newest Python.

practices.thinking: A plugin keeps code that more than one plugin needs once, in the plugin whose job that code does, such as Lane's hooks. The others take it in through a relative symbolic link, as installing copies a link's target into the plugin, which [symlinks in a marketplace](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/host-marketplace#share-files-within-a-marketplace-with-symlinks) documents.

steps.text: Run a check for copied code, such as `pylint --enable=duplicate-code`, over the marketplace's Python.

practices.thinking: Where another plugin already does a job, the plugin names it in `dependencies` of its `plugin.json`, and the plugin's deliverable names it in its preconditions, as Q1 says. Where one role of the other does the job, a route names the role as `<dependency>:<role>`, and the main conversation starts it as one of its own and puts its points to the person, while the other's guard holds its calls. Where the job is the other's whole run, a route names its skill as `<dependency>:<skill>`, and the main conversation calls the skill as one move, which ends once the other gives its result. Meanwhile the other's guard holds the conversation, and the plugin's own checks nothing, as two guards on one conversation would stop each other's moves.

steps.text: Name the dependency in `plugin.json`, and name its role or its skill in the routes that Q8 has the developer read in `lay.py print`.

practices.thinking: The caller decides what's theirs, and what's hard to undo, such as a merge. Such a point counts as approved only by the caller's own act, such as a skill the AI can't call. An AI that decides for the caller leaves them answerable for what they never saw, and an approval that an agent can give itself stops nothing.

steps.text: Set `disable-model-invocation: true` in the frontmatter of each skill that approves such a point.

practices.thinking: Where a plugin talks with a person, a role puts to them every point that only they can decide, one point a message, with a recommendation. It finds facts itself, and shows each fact the work rests on. It decides everything else, and reports it at the end. A point settled before the work doesn't come back as rework, and a question about what the person doesn't care about spends their time on the plugin's job, as [grilling](https://github.com/mattpocock/skills/blob/main/skills/productivity/grilling/SKILL.md) says.

steps.text: Write an architecture test that resumes the role with an answer, and check that its next message holds one point.

practices.thinking: When something outside the work stops it, the role asks for it, goes on with the rest meanwhile, and never looks for a way round. The person clears such a cause in a moment. A way round leaves the work checked on other terms than its purpose set.

steps.text: Write an architecture test whose double of Claude Code denies a call, and check that the role's message asks for it.

practices.thinking: Where a plugin talks with a person, it talks in the person's language, and writes the repository in the repository's language, English where it has none. It shows the person exactly what it writes. The person approves what they read, and others read the repository later.

Where the work's user gets something no machine can check, an evaluator, a role that didn't make the work, checks it first, given only what the user has. It answers each question as met, with the lines that meet it, or as not met, with what the user still lacks, never how to make it. A hunt for defects finds something in every work, and never ends. The maker holds the sources, so how to mend is its call, as [harness design](https://www.anthropic.com/engineering/harness-design-long-running-apps) says. Where the caller reads the whole work to approve it, such as a plan, no evaluator reads it first, as the caller is its first reader. Before the maker hands the work on, it answers each question the same way, as the work's user, with the lines that meet it or what the user still lacks. A lack that the maker could see costs a round of the evaluator to find, and the user waits longer for the work. Only the evaluator's answers count, as the maker reads what it meant, not what it wrote. The maker sends each shortfall back to the decision of the work's design that serves the question, such as a node of a design tree, and brings the work in line with the decisions. It lays no fix beside them. The design is the work's single source of truth, and a fix beside the design is a part that no decision holds. The next round loses it, or keeps it though no one settled it, and a fix for one finding can break a question that the evaluator found met. Where only a changed decision meets the shortfall, the maker names that decision for whoever settles the design, and leaves it as it stands, as a decision that the maker changes is one that no one settled.

steps.text: Give the evaluator's agent only the tools to read the work and write its answers, and lay a lane that holds it to reading only what the work's user has.

practices.thinking: Where a person calls the plugin, the main conversation looks once, after the caller approves the work, through what the run kept, for what fell short and why, quoting each cause from the records. It puts a lesson of the project's own into the project's rules, and sends a general lesson to the plugin's repository as an issue, only when the user says yes. A lesson met once improves every later run, and the user chooses what leaves their project.

steps.text: Have the skill's part read the run's records with Read before it ends, and quote each cause it names.

practices.thinking: The test levels are the [architecture best practice](../architecture/best-practice.md)'s. No level runs a prompt, a skill, or an agent alone on a model, as a trial of one role alone meets only the cases that its developer set up, and finds no fault that a real request brings out. Instead, the guard holds each rule of a role's steps that must hold on every run, and the architecture tests run the guard on each path, with a double in each role's place. The cost: a fault in a prompt shows only in a product vision trial.

steps.text: Write the architecture tests with a double of Claude Code that runs each hook's entry and script in the test's own process, as a new process of Python would run it, and sends what its documentation says or what a recorded try of the real Claude Code showed. Run them with the unit tests before each push.
Check each configuration written by hand, such as `hooks.json`, with `claude plugin validate`, as no test runs its commands.

Start each Claude Code of a product vision trial on a configuration folder of its own that holds only the plugins under test, with the developer's login as `CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN`, as [multiple accounts](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/authentication#log-in-with-multiple-accounts) says. The developer's own settings would change what the trial tries.
Have the stand-in answer each ask to allow a call from what the screen shows, as a person would.

practices.thinking: Each plugin and the marketplace pass Claude Code's own check of their manifests, as a malformed manifest fails every user at install.

steps.text: Run `claude plugin validate --strict` on the plugin and on the marketplace.

practices.thinking: A plugin gets a release only when whoever decides what reaches users says so. `plugin.json` holds `version` once, in [Semantic Versioning](https://semver.org), and the largest change that users see decides which part of it rises, as users get an update only when the version rises and `plugin.json` wins over the marketplace entry. The CHANGELOG gives each change that users notice one line, with why it helps them, as [Keep a Changelog](https://keepachangelog.com) does. Each release has a tag `<plugin>--v<version>`, as a dependency's version range resolves against these tags, and the marketplace and the root README list it.

steps.text: Tag each release by `claude plugin tag --push`.

practices.thinking: A would-be user reads the manifest's `description` in the listings of `/plugin` before they install, and decides by it whether the plugin is for them, as [display fields](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/plugins/marketplace-reference#display-fields) says. So it says in one sentence what a user achieves with the plugin, in the words of its product vision's users, as a value proposition does, and not what the plugin holds or how it works. A would-be user who reads only what the plugin holds can't tell whether it gets them what they're after. A marketplace entry's `description` wins over the manifest's, and Claude Code reads the manifest before install only where the entry's source is a relative path, so the description lies in one place: in the manifest where the source is a relative path, and in the entry otherwise. `README.md` is a deliverable of its own, of the kind [readme](../readme/best-practice.md), made from the plugin's product vision before the plugin's architecture. The plugin keeps it in its folder, so the README reaches each user with the plugin.

steps.text: Write the description from the opening of the plugin's product vision, and leave `description` out of the plugin's marketplace entry where its source is a relative path, so the two never differ.

practices.thinking: Claude Code picks a skill by the description in its entry's frontmatter, as [skills](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/skills#frontmatter-reference) says. It picks an agent by its description too, as [subagents](https://code.claude.com/docs/en/sub-agents#understand-automatic-delegation) says. The skill's description says what a run gives the person, and then when to use it, in the words a person asks for that work in, as [writing effective descriptions](https://platform.claude.com/docs/en/agents-and-tools/agent-skills/best-practices#writing-effective-descriptions) says. It speaks in the third person and puts the key use first, as Claude Code cuts a long description short in the list of skills. A person who doesn't know the command then still reaches a run, and the guard of Q9 with it. Each agent's description names the plugin it serves and the skill that alone starts it, such as `Started by rn's up alone`, and asks for no other use, such as `use proactively`. An agent that another conversation starts runs outside any run, so no route of Q8 follows its end, and its point for the person reaches no one who puts it to them.

steps.text: In a product vision trial of Q22, ask for the work in a user's own words, without the command, and check that the skill starts.

practices.thinking: Each practice is the ideal for the case it names. A plugin takes what its architecture calls for, and where it differs from a practice, its architecture says why. Read this best practice whole as [Q10 of the meta best practice](../meta/best-practice.md#q10) says. Once the product vision trial shows a plugin built by it closer to the goal, ship it, and mend each shortfall met in use where it lies: in the goal, the template, a question, or a practice.
